| # NVM block description {#nvm-block-description-1 .p_Heading1 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}                                                  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

 

The following tables shows all available NVM blocks which can be used by the application.

![hmtoggle_plus1](hmtoggle_plus1.gif){#toggle0186a1_ICON .dropdown-toggle-icon style="margin:0;width:0.1042in;height:0.0938in;border:none"} [FFI](javascript:HMToggle('toggle','toggle0186a1','toggle0186a1_ICON')){.dropdown-toggle style="font-style: normal; font-weight: normal; color: #002b49; background-color: transparent; text-decoration: none;"}

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NVM blocks of ID bds_mem_nvmBlock76_512_N_D, bds_mem_nvmBlock77_1024_N_D, bds_mem_nvmBlock78_1024_N_D and bds_mem_nvmBlock79_1024_N_D can be read/written/marked for writing by using \_ffi APIs for NVM when used in untrusted partition.
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

 

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ![Notice_RGB 39-153-209](hmfile_hash_c5013a84.png){style="margin:0;width:1.4792in;height:0.2813in;border:none"}   DFlash cells of the NVM have limited number of write cycles. The bds_mem_writeBlock function always stores all bytes of this block in the NVM independent on the real changed data. Therefore Data which are written more often should be located in blocks that are as small as possible.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
